repairs.name: The well's rotten rope
repairs.reaction: Bread tastes of the well again.
repairs.hint: The village well in the square
repairs.description: The well rope is rotten through; water cannot be drawn.
repairs.mendedDescription: A sound fibre rope hangs on the well. Water can be drawn again.

repairs.name: A fallen fence rail
repairs.reaction: The gap’s shut. Path was chewing into the grass.
repairs.hint: The garden fence below the square
repairs.description: A rail has fallen from the garden fence; the path cuts the corner.
repairs.mendedDescription: The split rail is pegged tight; the fence gap is closed.

repairs.name: The leaking library roof
repairs.reaction: The drip’s stopped. I’ve put the bucket away.
repairs.description: Slates slipped on the library roof; rain drips into the reading room.
repairs.mendedDescription: Fresh slates dressed and pinned; the drip bucket is gone.

repairs.name: A bench with a cracked slat
repairs.reaction: That’s a true slat. Good oak.
repairs.hint: The bench by the square's lamp
repairs.description: A cracked slat on the village bench; you can't sit there.
repairs.mendedDescription: A smooth oak slat pegged into the bench; you can sit there again.

repairs.name: A guttering village lamp
repairs.hint: The village lamp beside the well
repairs.description: The village lamp gutters in the draft; the wick is burned down.
repairs.mendedDescription: A fresh wick trimmed and lit; the lamp burns steady and warm.

repairs.name: The hame before Carting Day
repairs.reaction: Shines the way Hollis kept it.
repairs.hint: The horse collar on the Commons gate
repairs.description: The empty carter's collar on the gate has weathered dull.
repairs.mendedDescription: Polished with oilcloth; the brass hame shines on the gate.
